evals.prompt: With the shotgun out in training, does OpenFAKK2's crosshair look like retail's when Julie aims at the floor? Show me both.
evals.expected_output: A probe (probe-crosshair.scr or an equivalent) that waits for the player, outlasts the training intro, gives and wields the shotgun with a hand argument, holds +lookdown briefly and takes screenshots, ending with quit; a capture.ps1 run on both games; a report that names the pair image, describes how the crosshair is drawn in each (flat on the floor in retail) and gives the difference figures.
expectations: The probe starts with waitforplayer and waits long enough to outlast the training intro (about 25 s) before giving the weapon
The probe selects the weapon with a hand argument (use Shotgun dual) and pitches the view down with +lookdown / -lookdown before a screenshot

The probe was run on both games through capture.ps1 (or the same probe through both runners), with no +wait on either command line, so build\compare\captures\<probe>-training holds retail and ours shots of the same moment
The report says where the crosshair lies in each picture (retail draws it flat on the floor) and gives the difference figures or the pair image as evidence
The report does not treat the small view shift from key timing as a rendering difference

evals.prompt: Did my renderer change alter how the swamp branches look in swamp1? Compare this build with the main checkout's build, and with retail.
evals.expected_output: Three captures of probe-swbranch on swamp1 from its script cameras: retail, this build, and the main checkout's build (via -Bin and -Name before); a report that compares each build with retail using the difference figures and says whether the change moved the picture towards or away from retail.
expectations: The capture uses script cameras (probe-swbranch.scr or an equivalent spawn Camera / cuecamera probe) so the views match exactly
One OpenFAKK2 capture uses the main checkout's build (-Bin pointing under the main checkout's build folder) with a distinct -Name, and one uses this worktree's build
Retail was captured with the same probe
The report gives difference figures for each build against retail, taken from the runner's output or shots.py, and its verdict follows from them
Neither run put +wait on the command line or used an edited copy of the probe without waitforplayer

evals.prompt: Do the health and water gauges match retail at 50 health and 50 water?
evals.expected_output: A capture of probe-hud (or a probe setting $player health 50 and $player waterpower 50 before a screenshot) on training on both games, and a zoomed pair of the gauge region with shots.py pair --crop --zoom, with a verdict.
expectations: The probe sets the state with script lines ($player health 50, $player waterpower 50) rather than cheat cvars
Both games were captured with the same probe
The comparison crops to the gauges in the top-left corner (shots.py pair --crop ... --zoom) rather than judging the whole frame
The verdict names what differs in the gauges, if anything, with the zoomed pair as evidence, and discounts the notify line or masks it
